caption: Psalm 16 is a strong candidate for John’s unnamed resurrection Scripture because Acts explicitly uses it that way. John itself never identifies the passage.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Is Psalm 16 John’s resurrection Scripture? The psalm speaks of escape from the grave and a path of life. John says Scripture required Jesus to rise.
slides.body: The psalm speaks of escape from the grave and a path of life. John says Scripture required Jesus to rise.
slides.heading: Is Psalm 16 John’s resurrection Scripture?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 16:9-11: You will not abandon my soul to Sheol … You have made known to me the path of life.
slides.body: You will not abandon my soul to Sheol … You have made known to me the path of life.
slides.heading: Ps 16:9-11

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 20:9, BSB: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
slides.body: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 20:9

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Acts makes the link explicit Two speeches in Acts quote this psalm about Jesus’s resurrection. It is a strong candidate for John’s unnamed Scripture.
slides.body: Two speeches in Acts quote this psalm about Jesus’s resurrection. It is a strong candidate for John’s unnamed Scripture.
slides.heading: Acts makes the link explicit

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But John never names the passage The psalm may describe rescue from death. Its specific resurrection meaning comes through Acts’s later argument.
